options.name: solve_mode
options.doc:
Gauss-Seidel sweep order of the matrix-free solve, which never assembles the Delassus matrix: it recomputes J v every iteration and uses only the diagonal for preconditioning. "serial" (default) sweeps each world's rows in order in one fused kernel. "colored" colors the propagation contact rows every step so that no two rows of a color share a responding body (a kinematic free body has no response and may be shared) and solves each color as one parallel launch across all worlds; contacts left without a color run last, in the order set by propagation_color_order. "colored" covers free bodies as well as articulations and requires articulated_contact_response="propagation"; any other response raises ValueError. On CPU both modes run world-serial portable kernels ("colored" sweeps in serial order), and the CUDA-only features listed in the class description raise NotImplementedError.

Deprecated 1.8. "matrix_free" maps to "serial", and "split", whose dense Delassus solve was removed, runs "serial"; each emits a NewtonDeprecationWarning.
options.when: Use "colored" (with the propagation response) for worlds with many free bodies, such as piles and pours. Keep "serial" for articulated robots, small scenes and loop closures.

options.name: iterations
options.doc: Number of projected Gauss-Seidel iterations per step.
options.when: Raise for tall stacks, large mass ratios, loop closures and slipping grasps. Lower only after a full-episode check passes at the lower value.

options.name: baumgarte
options.doc: Baumgarte position-correction factor of contact and joint-limit rows, as a fraction of the position error removed per step.
options.when: Up to 0.5 for light bodies pressed into the ground by heavy ones. Higher values launched bodies in testing; prefer velocity_iterations for deep start overlaps.

options.name: cfm
options.doc: Constraint force mixing added to every row's effective-mass diagonal, which regularizes redundant rows. Drive rows of drive_mode="rows" use their exact unit response instead, and the coupled contact solves of a friction_mode other than "fixed_normal" leave it off their contact blocks.
options.when: Rarely changed. It regularizes redundant rows such as closures and coplanar contacts.

options.name: relaxation
options.doc: Successive over-relaxation factor of the PGS sweep.
options.when: Leave at 1. Under-relaxation (about 0.6) helped one momentum-accelerated rope; values above 1 made a heavy impactor sink further.

options.name: update_mass_matrix_interval
options.doc: Rebuild and refactor the mass matrix every this many calls to step; 1 rebuilds it every step. Larger values reuse a stale factorization between rebuilds. A change of dt, reset and notify_model_changed still request a refresh of the affected articulations. Under CUDA graph capture the host-side cadence is baked into the graph, so the interval should divide the number of steps captured per graph.
options.when: Above 1 only for slowly moving articulations; it must divide the steps per captured graph.

options.name: enable_joint_limits
options.doc: Enforce joint_limit_lower and joint_limit_upper of PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE and D6 DOFs as unilateral rows. When False (the default), no joint-limit rows are created, joint position limits are not enforced, and limits use no articulation_constraint_max capacity. The default matches the Steel reference implementation this solver is ported from.
options.when: Set True whenever the model authors joint limits. Off, limits are not simulated.

options.name: joint_limit_activation_gap
options.doc: Distance from a finite position limit [m or rad] at which its row is created, when enable_joint_limits is set. inf creates the rows of every finite limit each step; a smaller gap creates a row only when q <= lower + gap or q >= upper - gap. None (the default) uses a speed-aware gap of 0.05 + 2 * dt * |v| per DOF, where v is the joint's unconstrained velocity at the end of the step, after drives, gravity and parent motion. Limit rows are speculative and apply no impulse while the joint cannot reach its bound within the step, so the skipped rows are no-ops unless constraint impulses in the solve, such as contacts, accelerate the joint toward the bound by more than the margin in one step. Mimic and connect rows also act inside the solve, so both mimic ends, the tree joints between the two ends of each mimic or loop closure, and every joint below them always have their rows. Joints above a closure's common ancestor carry both ends and stay gated, which can miss a passive limited mount under opposed mimics. With drive_mode="rows" the drives act inside the solve too, so None creates every limit row, as inf does. A bound at or beyond MAXVAL, the builder's unlimited default (+/-1e10), has no row. The constructor warns when the finite limits alone exceed the capacity. The value is validated even when joint limits are disabled.
options.when: A fixed gap such as 0.1 builds limit rows only near a limit and is often faster than the speed-aware default. Keep it above 2 * max|qd| * dt.

options.name: enable_joint_velocity_limits
options.doc: Enforce joint_velocity_limit of PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE and D6 DOFs with one row pair per limited DOF, after scaling articulation velocities that already exceed a limit. A DOF at the builder's default limit (1e6) or above has no rows. The free-body limits of register_custom_attributes are enforced whenever those attributes are registered, independently of this option.
options.when: Set True when the task depends on joint velocity limits.

options.name: velocity_limit_activation_fraction
options.doc: Create the velocity-limit rows of a DOF only when |qd| >= velocity_limit_activation_fraction * limit. 0 creates them for every limited DOF each step; inf never creates them. The gate samples the velocity before the solve, so a DOF that crosses the threshold during a step is clamped one step later. Must be in [0, 1] or inf.
options.when: Raise toward 1 to skip rows of DOFs far below their limit.

options.name: enable_joint_friction
options.doc:
Enforce joint_friction [N or N·m] as dry joint friction (MuJoCo frictionloss). Each PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE, BALL or D6 DOF with positive friction adds one row whose impulse is bounded by joint_friction * dt around a zero-velocity target, so the DOF sticks until the required effort exceeds the friction and then slides against it. A BALL joint's three DOFs are separate boxes about the axes of its angular velocity coordinates. The rows use the articulated response, so coupled inertia, armature, drives, limits and contacts act jointly; their impulses cold-start each step and count against articulation_constraint_max. The coefficients are read and checked on the device every step, also on graph replay, so in-place edits take effect on the next step. An eager step reads a replaced array; a captured graph keeps the array it was captured with, so recapture after replacing it. After editing or replacing the coefficients, call notify_model_changed with JOINT_DOF_PROPERTIES (or the narrower JOINT_DOF_FORCE_PROPERTIES) to wake sleeping islands whose friction changed. Non-finite or negative values, and nonzero friction on other joint types or loop-closing joints, are invalid: such a DOF builds no row, construction and eager notifications raise ValueError, and steps flag the owning world for check_constraint_capacity. Requires CUDA and is not supported with contact_compliance or enable_bilateral_preelimination; those combinations raise NotImplementedError. Enabling it disables the articulation-local, paired factor-coordinate and sparse-diagonal solves and sparse mass factors at construction, even when every coefficient is zero, so enable it only for models that need friction. When False, joint_friction is ignored.

A positive steel:joint_friction_load_coefficient at construction (see register_custom_attributes) adds load-proportional friction: each step, a DOF's bound grows by its coefficient times the load its joint transmits under that step's free dynamics. The row is solved together with the drives, so it resists a drive up to its bound, whereas PhysX applies the friction before each DOF's drive in every iteration and a stiff drive largely overrides it. With drive_mode="augmented" the implicit drive forces are part of the free dynamics and count toward the load; drive_mode="rows" leaves them out, as PhysX does. The coefficients follow the validity rules and notify contract of joint_friction. A model built with every coefficient zero must keep them zero; to randomize coefficients after construction, make at least one positive beforehand.

Experimental.enable_joint_friction and its supported combinations may change without the normal deprecation period.
options.when: Set True for models that author joint friction (MJCF frictionloss). It disables several fast paths, so leave it off otherwise.

options.name: articulation_constraint_max
options.doc: Capacity of rows involving articulated bodies (mimic and connect rows, contacts, enabled joint limits, joint velocity limits, joint friction and, with drive_mode="rows", joint drives) per world. Rows beyond it are dropped and reported, see constraint_overflow.
options.when: Size from row_watermark: about 2x the requested mark while overflowing, then 1.3x a non-overflowing mark. Robots with limits or self-contacts often need more than 32.

options.name: free_body_constraint_max
options.doc: Capacity of free-body rows per world: free-body contact rows and free-body velocity-limit rows. Under the "propagation" response free-body contacts use the propagation rows, so it sizes only the velocity-limit rows. Rows beyond it are dropped and reported, see constraint_overflow.
options.when: Size from row_watermark under the immediate response. Very large values stop the immediate kernels from building; move such scenes to colored propagation.

options.name: propagation_constraint_max
options.doc: Capacity of the propagation row family per world in the "propagation" response, which holds every contact row except those between two links of one articulation; these stay dense unless propagation_same_articulation_rows is set. None (default) uses free_body_constraint_max + articulation_constraint_max. Setting it lets free_body_constraint_max shrink to the free-body velocity-limit rows. At least 1; rejected with articulated_contact_response="immediate".
options.when: Size from row_watermark under the propagation response.

options.name: warn_constraint_overflow
options.doc: Print a device-side warning the first time a world exceeds a row capacity. The warning does not synchronize the host and is compatible with CUDA graph capture. The host contact torsion preparation emits its overflow warning as a NewtonWarning through warnings instead.
options.when: Turn off only when you check constraint_overflow yourself.

options.name: row_watermark
options.doc: Accumulate the high-water marks of the per-world row counts of every row family and of the contact count on the device in every step, including captured ones; read them with constraint_row_watermarks.
options.when: On while tuning. Read constraint_row_watermarks() after a full episode.

options.name: drive_mode
options.doc: Joint drive formulation. "augmented" integrates drives implicitly in the mass matrix. "rows" adds one dense PGS row per driven DOF (positive joint_target_ke or joint_target_kd) whose impulse follows the PhysX articulation force-drive update in every iteration, so drives are solved together with contacts and limits instead of before them. Without contacts or limits and below the effort limit, the converged row reproduces the implicit drive of "augmented". Under effort saturation the two differ: "augmented" clamps the explicit drive force before the implicit solve, while the row clamps its accumulated impulse at joint_effort_limit * dt. Drive rows are allocated first in each world, count against articulation_constraint_max, and a drive whose row does not fit is not applied (the world is flagged in constraint_overflow).
options.when: "rows" when drive torques must respect the effort limit exactly (torque-limited robots, sim-to-real), or to solve drives together with contacts.

options.name: fuse_joint_velocity_limits
options.doc: With drive_mode="rows" and enable_joint_velocity_limits, enforce the velocity limit of each driven DOF with a clamp of its velocity at the end of every iteration (after the contact rows, like the velocity-limit rows it replaces) instead of two velocity-limit rows, and exclude it from the pre-solve velocity scaling. Limited DOFs without a drive row keep their rows. In every other configuration, including velocity_limit_activation_fraction=inf, the option has no effect; velocity_limits_fused reports whether the clamp is active.
options.when: Leave on; set False to keep explicit velocity-limit rows on driven DOFs.

options.name: enable_bilateral_preelimination
options.doc: Eliminate the mimic and connect rows of each articulation before the iterative sweep with a Schur complement of the bilateral block S = J_B H^-1 J_B^T: the predicted velocity is projected once and the responses of the other rows are corrected, so closures and mimic couplings depend much less on iterations. The block is factored with a diagonal regularization R of 1e-3 times each row's diagonal plus a floor of max(cfm, 1e-7), which keeps nearly dependent closure axes positive definite. The elimination is therefore not exact: a bilateral velocity residual of R (S + R)^-1 (J_B v + b_B) remains after the projection, and the corrected responses of other rows still couple into the bilateral rows by the same factor. The rows stay allocated and in the sweep, which reduces this residual further. If any articulation owns more than eight bilateral rows (a FIXED loop closure, such as a link-break weld, takes six), any loop closure has a kinematic or world parent, or velocity_iterations is positive, elimination is disabled for the whole solver (every articulation keeps iterative rows) with a warning at construction.
options.when: Loop closures or mimic couplings that drift at your iteration budget.

options.name: bilateral_preelimination_include_mimics
options.doc: With pre-elimination enabled, also eliminate mimic rows. False eliminates only the connect rows and keeps mimic rows iterative, which avoids a singular block when a mimic row is nearly dependent on a closure.
options.when: Set False if a mimic row is nearly dependent on a closure and the eliminated block becomes singular.

options.name: parallel_tree
options.doc: Traverse the independent branches of each articulation tree in parallel (forward kinematics and dynamics, the inverse-dynamics backward pass and state publication), with up to 32 threads per articulation instead of one. Results match the serial traversal up to floating-point summation order. Unbranched articulations, models whose joints are not ordered parent before child, and CPU devices keep the serial traversal. Broad trees can benefit; narrow trees can be slower, so measure the full step before enabling it.
options.when: Broad trees such as hands; time the full step before keeping it.

options.name: reuse_kinematics
options.doc: Opt in to carrying the kinematics and inverse-dynamics terms the solver forms when it publishes a step's body state into the next step, instead of re-deriving them from the joint coordinates. The carry runs on CUDA only and stays off with gradients, joint velocity limits, sleeping, the parallel tree, or a FREE or DISTANCE joint that is not the first joint of its articulation; the attribute of the same name reports whether it runs. Off by default: every step then re-derives the kinematics from its input state and publishes through eval_fk, as before. With the carry on, the terms belong to the state object they were published into: reset drops them for the selected worlds, notify_model_changed drops them for joint, body and model property changes, a coupler's input-state notice drops them, and a step whose input state is another object recomputes them; a caller that overwrites or replaces joint_q, joint_qd or body_q of that state outside step must call notify_state_changed (or reset with a world mask) first. The published body poses and velocities then come from the solver's own kinematics and can differ from eval_fk's in their last bit.
options.when: Time it on your scene; call notify_state_changed after writing state outside step().

options.name: use_parallel_streams
options.doc: Run the factorization, unconstrained solve and response kernels of each articulation-size group on a CUDA stream of its own, so groups of different sizes overlap. Results are unchanged; CPU devices and models with one size group ignore it.
options.when: Models with several articulation sizes, or many independent single-DOF joints on one base.

options.name: double_buffer
options.doc: Keep two sets of the grouped mass-matrix and Jacobian buffers and clear the set a step used on a separate CUDA stream, which the step joins before it returns. Results are unchanged; CPU devices and the sparse mass factors ignore it. Steps and graph launches of one solver must be ordered on one stream (or through explicit stream dependencies).
options.when: Time it on your scene; results are unchanged.

options.name: friction_anchor_beta
options.doc: Position-correction gain of persistent friction patches; 0 selects point friction. None selects 0.2, and point friction when contact_compliance is enabled or friction_mode is not "fixed_normal". With a positive gain, the contacts of a body pair whose normals, contact planes and friction coefficients agree and whose shapes touch form a region. Each region's friction acts at up to two anchors along its principal extent, which share the region's total normal impulse; every contact keeps its own normal row. An anchor carries its tangential displacement across steps, following the pose increments of both bodies, and the tangent rows add friction_anchor_beta * displacement / dt, so a held object does not creep under a static load. Anchors are released when their region is unloaded or slides at the Coulomb limit; history is matched by body pair and geometry, independently of collision contact matching. A one-anchor region has no torsional friction of its own. Call reset after teleporting a body to discard its history.
options.when: Keep the default (anchors) for anything held, carried or pinched. Set 0 (point friction) for scenes where nothing is held; it is cheaper.

options.name: contact_regularization
options.doc: Dimensionless regularization g of penetrating contact rows (friction_mode="fixed_normal" only). Each iteration moves a row's impulse toward the rigid solution with weight 1 / (1 + g) and toward zero with weight g / (1 + g), the update of an implicitly integrated contact spring. It makes statically indeterminate normal-force splits unique and damps the sweep, at the cost of a resting penetration: a row at rest settles at baumgarte * phi / dt = -g * d * lambda (d its unsplit inverse effective mass, lambda its impulse), about g * a * dt^2 / baumgarte for a body under acceleration a resting on one row. Propagation rows whose response is split across coupled contact bodies, with split diagonal d_s, take weight w * d_s / (w * d_s + (1 - w) * d) with w = 1 / (1 + g), which reaches the same rest state. Speculative (positive-gap) rows, rows whose rebound fires and the velocity-only iterations stay rigid. 0 is the rigid law; at most 1e6.
options.when: About 0.01 removes warm-start bursts on deeply wedged contacts and makes indeterminate load splits unique, at a small resting penetration.

options.name: velocity_iterations
options.doc: Number of velocity-only iterations after the position solve. Positions are integrated from the position solve; these iterations then refine the velocity without the position bias, so stabilization does not add velocity to the bodies. A positive-gap contact whose linearized gap at the end of the step stays open keeps its speculative allowance, and an impacting contact keeps its rebound target.
options.when: Set 2 to 4 when position correction launches bodies (deep start overlaps). Must be 0 with sleeping, compliance, and torsion under propagation.

options.name: velocity_drive_mode
options.doc: Treatment of PGS joint-drive rows during the velocity-only iterations: "freeze" keeps the drive impulses of the position solve, "active" keeps solving the drive rows. Implicit (mass-matrix) drives have no rows, so the option has no effect for them.
options.when: Only matters with drive_mode="rows" and velocity_iterations > 0.

options.name: row_schedule
options.doc: Row order of the matrix-free sweeps. "interleaved" sweeps every row family in each iteration: the dense rows, the free-body contact rows, then the velocity limits. "contact_then_internal" runs every iteration of the contact rows first, then every iteration of the internal rows (drive, mimic, connect, joint-limit and joint-friction rows) and the velocity limits. "phased" approximates the order PhysX uses for grasping: each iteration solves the internal rows, then the contact rows, then the velocity limits, each in a launch of its own; the propagation responses use this order with "interleaved" as well. Contact torsion and contact compliance require "interleaved", and the sparse mass factors are selected only with "interleaved".
options.when: Try "phased" for grasps tuned against PhysX. Contact torsion, compliance and the sparse mass factors need "interleaved".

options.name: friction_mode
options.doc: Experimental Coulomb friction update of the matrix-free solve. "fixed_normal" updates both tangent impulses together on the friction disk of the current normal impulse: sticking uses the inverse of their 2x2 block, sliding a bounded scalar solve that keeps isotropic maximum dissipation. "bisection" bisects the normal impulse of each contact and re-solves the 2x2 tangent problem at every probe, so normal and friction impulses are updated together. "bisection_desaxce" adds the de Saxce maximum-dissipation bias mu * |c_T| to the normal target velocity of free-body contacts (Le Lidec and Carpentier, 2024). "coulomb_newton" solves each free-body contact's Coulomb cone exactly with a bracketed scalar Newton iteration on the tangential-force ratio; articulated contacts keep the "fixed_normal" update. The other modes replace each contact's normal and friction impulses with their coupled solution, which relaxation does not scale, and use point friction: an omitted friction_anchor_beta selects it with a warning, and friction patches, contact torsion, contact compliance, contact_regularization and articulated_contact_response="propagation" with solve_mode="serial" require "fixed_normal". The free-body and articulated rules above apply to articulated_contact_response="immediate". solve_mode="colored" solves every contact on a propagation row, articulated ones included, with the free-body update of the selected mode; contacts between two links of one articulation stay on dense rows and keep the articulated update. This option may change without the normal deprecation period.
options.when: Experimental. Leave at "fixed_normal" unless you are studying the coupled Coulomb solve.

options.name: contact_warmstart
options.doc: Start each step from the previous step's contact impulses, matched by contact identity through rigid_contact_match_index, so the CollisionPipeline must be created with contact matching enabled. Substeps that reuse a contact set without a collision pass seed each contact from its own previous substep. History carries across one collision pass into the same Contacts buffer when that pass matched against the solved contact set (rigid_contact_match_generation); a different buffer, skipped passes, or a pass after the pipeline wrote another buffer start cold. Carried impulses are scaled by the ratio of the step to the previous one, including under graph replay; tangent impulses are rotated into the current tangent frame and clamped to the current friction cone; other rows start cold. The pipeline's default matching compares world-space contact midpoints, so contacts that two bodies carry together farther than contact_matching_pos_threshold per step can lose their match and start cold; contact_matching_body_frame=True also matches them in their bodies' frames.
options.when: Off by default. Turn on only where a measured scene needs it (for example a house of cards with momentum). Needs contact matching; never for a grasp without anchors.

options.name: contact_warmstart_decay
options.doc: Non-negative scale applied to the carried impulses.
options.when: Values below 1 weaken the carried impulses of warm start.

options.name: enable_restitution
options.doc: Apply contact restitution, the only restitution switch. The default True leaves the shapes' coefficients in charge; they default to zero, so a model that authors no restitution does not bounce. False turns restitution off for every contact regardless of the coefficients, and lets contact_compliance accept shapes with positive restitution.
options.when: Set False to ignore authored restitution everywhere, or to use contact_compliance with shapes that author restitution.

options.name: restitution_velocity_threshold
options.doc: Minimum closing speed [m/s] of a contact at the start of the step for a rebound. Contacts bounce with the two shapes' restitution coefficients combined by restitution_combine (restitution, clamped to [0, 1]; zero gives no rebound): an impacting contact replaces its position bias by the rebound target -e * u_start, where u_start is its relative normal velocity at the start of the step, as a lower bound on its separating velocity. The contact must also touch, or be predicted to reach the surface during the step. Slower contacts keep the ordinary contact law, so a resting contact pressed by gravity, a drive or an applied force does not bounce, and this step's forces do not enlarge a rebound. Finite and non-negative.
options.when: Lower to let slower impacts bounce; raise to make slow impacts inelastic.

options.name: contact_speculative_scale
options.doc: Fraction of a positive contact gap that the contact may close during the step (rhs = scale * phi / dt). 0 removes the speculative allowance; penetration correction is unchanged.
options.when: Rarely changed. 1 lets a contact close exactly its gap in one step; 0 removes the speculative allowance.

options.name: contact_gap_gate
options.doc: Contacts of the collision pipeline whose gap [m] exceeds this distance get no rows; 0 keeps touching contacts only. None (the default) keeps every contact. gap decides which contacts the pipeline reports (also to sensors and other solvers); this gate only decides which of them this solver solves. Finite and non-negative.
options.when: Set 0 where speculative rows never engage (for example many small rollers) to save rows.

options.name: contact_friction_scale
options.doc: Non-negative factor applied to every shape's friction coefficient (shape_material_mu) in the solver's copy of the materials, refreshed at construction and by notify_model_changed with SHAPE_PROPERTIES. It scales the friction rows, patches and the torsion budget; the model's coefficients are unchanged.
options.when: Sweeps or domain randomization over friction without editing shape materials.

options.name: contact_friction_position_iterations
options.doc: Number of position iterations that solve tangential friction rows. -1 (the default) solves them in every position iteration; k >= 0 solves them only in the last k position iterations (0 never), and holds their impulses at zero before that. Velocity-only iterations always solve friction. Values other than -1 reject contact_warmstart and contact_compliance.
options.when: Rarely changed. Solves friction only in the last k position iterations; rejects warm start and compliance.

options.name: contact_friction_gap_max
options.doc: Contacts with a gap [m] above this distance get a normal row only. None (the default) gives every contact friction rows; -inf gives none of them friction rows, which saves the rows that zero friction coefficients would keep. A finite negative value keeps friction rows for contacts that penetrate deeper than it. Switching between None (or inf) and a finite or -inf value requires a new solver.
options.when: -inf for a frictionless scene, which saves the friction rows.

options.name: contact_shared_anchor
options.doc: Apply every contact row at the midpoint of the two witness points instead of at each body's own witness point, as PhysX applies a contact at one point. phi still comes from the witness points. Friction patch rows keep their patch anchors, so with patches this moves only the normal rows.
options.when: Match PhysX's single-point contact application.

options.name: contact_friction_shared_anchor
options.doc: Apply the friction rows at the witness midpoint, which removes the tangential force couple of witness points separated along the normal. It has no effect on friction patch rows, which act at their anchors.
options.when: Remove the friction couple of witness points separated along the normal.

options.name: contact_torsion_device
options.doc: Experimental contact torsion is enabled at construction when any shape has a positive steel:min_torsional_patch_radius (see register_custom_attributes). It adds one angular row per contact group of an articulated body, about the group's normal, bounded by r * (mu * N - sliding): sliding and spin share one Coulomb budget, N is the final solved load of the group's normal rows, and r is the largest radius of the group's shapes (a patch region can span several shape pairs; contacts whose pair has no positive radius get no torsion). With point friction a group is a coplanar cluster of touching contacts of one shape pair; with friction patches it is one patch region, budgeted by its pooled load and undivided friction coefficient. The radius is an effective footprint, not derived from the geometry: for uniform pressure on a disk of radius R it is 2 * R / 3. Rows are rebuilt every step and carry no spin history; free-body contacts get none. Supported geometry is sphere, box, capsule, cylinder, cone, ellipsoid, plane and convex mesh. Requires contact_warmstart=False; contacts with hydroelastic stiffness are rejected. Dense torsion rows count against articulation_constraint_max after the world's other dense rows. A world whose groups do not all fit keeps the rows that fit, and a world that dropped dense rows gets no dense torsion rows; both set the world's constraint_overflow entry and warn when warn_constraint_overflow is set, and other worlds step unaffected. contact_torsion_device prepares the torsion rows on the device instead of on the host. The host preparation is the reference implementation; it reads the contacts back every step and cannot be captured in a CUDA graph. The device preparation builds the same groups and rows with preallocated buffers and supports CUDA graph capture of step. Invalid torsion input (contact-buffer overflow, hydroelastic contacts, or a friction-patch load ring that does not match its group) makes an eager step raise before it applies torsion rows. In a captured step the error is deferred: the failing step restores its output motion arrays (joint_q, joint_qd, body_q, body_qd, body_qdd) to the input values, while other outputs, observables and solver history still advance, and check_constraint_capacity raises after the replays. Check before using replay results, discard failed output, fix the cause and reset. The input error is solver-wide: any reset clears it, and a cause that persists latches it again on the next step. Grouping runs serially per world with worst-case quadratic cost in the contacts of a world. No effect without contact torsion. With articulated_contact_response="propagation", every positive-radius contact on an articulated body that is routed to propagation reserves one more propagation row for torsion (same-articulation contacts stay dense unless propagation_same_articulation_rows is set), so size propagation_constraint_max, or articulation_constraint_max and free_body_constraint_max when it is unset, for it. A group's torsion row takes that row of its last member. The serial sweep solves the torsion rows after the other rows; the colored sweep solves each in its last member's contact unit, after the rows of the group's other members. Both use the same budget, and both solve modes require contact_torsion_device=True and velocity_iterations=0. solve_mode="colored" rejects contact torsion with contact_compliance, whose contacts are hydroelastic. When propagation rows overflow, a group keeps the contacts that received rows and the step does not raise: it sets constraint_overflow, warns when warn_constraint_overflow is set, and check_constraint_capacity raises.
options.when: Set True whenever shapes author steel:min_torsional_patch_radius and you capture CUDA graphs or use the propagation response.

options.name: contact_compliance
options.doc: Experimental: solve contacts that carry a positive rigid_contact_stiffness [N/m] with an implicit unilateral spring-damper law instead of the rigid normal law. The material comes from the contacts (per-shape hydroelastic stiffness, the contact damping [N s/m], zero staying zero, and the friction weight, applied once to the pair friction); contacts with zero stiffness stay rigid. A compliant row's force is max(0, -k phi_next - c u_next), solved with the residual u + k phi / (dt k + c) + lambda / (dt (dt k + c)) in every sweep; the damping term is dropped while the gap is open. Requires point friction (None or 0 for friction_anchor_beta; None warns), positive iterations, no warm start, no velocity-only iterations, no contact regularization, no shared anchors and zero shape restitution. With solve_mode="colored" the colored sweep solves the compliant rows, without contact torsion; "propagation" with solve_mode="serial" rejects it. The contacts must carry the hydroelastic material arrays. The rows are prepared on the device, so step can be captured in a CUDA graph. Invalid input (for example a compliant contact lost to a row capacity, even with warn_constraint_overflow off, or a positive shape restitution) makes an eager step raise. In a captured step the error is deferred: check_constraint_capacity raises after the replays, until reset, and their results are invalid; eager steps do not report it. Contacts the allocator excludes on purpose are counted in compliance_skipped_contact_count and compliant contacts in compliance_contact_count. This option may change without the normal deprecation period.
options.when: Experimental. Soft fingertips or pads modeled with hydroelastic contacts.

options.name: enable_sleeping
options.doc: Experimental passive-island sleeping. Articulations in contact are joined into islands every step. Static geometry and articulations with no responding degrees of freedom (such as a body welded to the world) support an island without joining it. A fixed-base articulation with responding joints, such as a robot arm, joins the island of everything it touches, so it can connect them into one island; its fixed root supports that island. A supported island whose bodies stay below sleep_linear_threshold and sleep_angular_threshold for sleep_quiet_time falls asleep, and its published state (joint_q, joint_qd, body_q, body_qd and, when requested, body_parent_f) is frozen until a wake event: a nonzero or nonfinite external force (body_f, joint_f), a changed state or gravity, a contact with an awake or moving body, lost support or row capacity, a reset of its world, or notify_model_changed for properties of its joints, DOFs, bodies or shapes (other notifications and changes to static or kinematic owners wake every island). Driven articulations (nonzero drive gains) and articulations with passive springs (nonzero joint_stiffness on a PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE or D6 tree joint) stay awake. Sleeping is configured at construction; rebuild captured graphs to change it. Construction raises ValueError with contact_warmstart or velocity_iterations, or for a model without articulations, and NotImplementedError with articulated_contact_response="propagation" and solve_mode="serial", and with solve_mode="colored" on CPU, where the colored mode runs the serial propagation sweep; with solve_mode="colored" on CUDA skipped islands are left out of the coloring, the colored sweep and the propagation trees, and, where CUDA conditional graph nodes are supported, a captured step in which every articulation that can sleep sleeps skips the propagation solve. step raises ValueError for a nonpositive or nonfinite dt and when state_in and state_out share arrays. The sleeping options are runtime solver settings with no USD schema.
options.when: Settling scenes with many passive objects. Excludes warm start and velocity iterations.

options.name: sleep_linear_threshold
options.doc: Body center-of-mass speed below which a body is quiet [m/s], finite and positive.
options.when: Lower if bodies fall asleep while still creeping.

options.name: sleep_angular_threshold
options.doc: Body angular speed below which a body is quiet [rad/s], finite and positive.
options.when: Lower if slowly spinning bodies fall asleep.

options.name: sleep_quiet_time
options.doc: Quiet, supported interval after which an island sleeps [s], finite and positive.
options.when: Raise if islands fall asleep before they settle.

options.name: sleep_skip_constraints
options.doc: Skip the work of sleeping islands: their contact and joint-limit rows (collision still runs, so wake events are complete), the rebuild of their friction-patch history (carried instead), and their articulated dynamics (kinematics, inverse dynamics, drives, mass matrix and factorization, velocity prediction and integration). False keeps the rows and dynamics of sleeping islands and only freezes their published state.
options.when: Set False when consumers read contact forces of sleeping bodies.

options.name: articulated_contact_response
options.doc:
How contacts touching an articulation that is not a free body are solved.

  • "immediate": dense rows of the articulation's generalized coordinates, Y = H^-1 J^T per row.
  • "propagation": fixed-size rows of the touched bodies at their centers of mass, with each body's 6x6 response from the articulated-body factorization of its tree. Each iteration solves these rows and then propagates the accumulated body impulses through the trees to the joint velocities. All contacts, including those of free bodies, use these rows, whose capacity per world is propagation_constraint_max, or free_body_constraint_max + articulation_constraint_max when that is None. With solve_mode="colored" each sweep solves the contacts of a world in batches of contacts that share no responding body, one batch after the other.

The propagation response avoids the per-row H^-1 J^T of contact rows at the cost of tree passes over every articulation in each iteration; which response is faster depends on the model. They keep joint-limit and velocity-limit rows dense, and contacts between two links of the same articulation dense unless propagation_same_articulation_rows is set. The tree factorization is rebuilt every step, independently of update_mass_matrix_interval.

Deprecated 1.8. "propagation_colored" maps to solve_mode="colored" with "propagation" and emits a NewtonDeprecationWarning.
options.when: "propagation" is required by the colored sweep. Keep "immediate" for loop-closing joints, Nesterov momentum and coupled solvers.

options.name: propagation_same_articulation_rows
options.doc: Solve contacts between two links of the same articulation as propagation rows, with the exact cross response of the two links, instead of dense rows. Requires articulated_contact_response="propagation" (either solve_mode).
options.when: Robots with many self-contacts under the propagation response, to move those contacts off the dense rows.

options.name: propagation_cached_response
options.doc: With articulated_contact_response="propagation" (either solve_mode), replace the per-iteration tree walk by cached responses: the setup extracts, for each contact-active body, its joint-space response R (DOFs x 6) and the 6x6 response blocks between active bodies, from the tree factorization that is fixed for the step, and each iteration applies them as a small matrix-vector product. The result equals the tree walk up to float reassociation. It applies to articulation groups with 0- or 1-DOF joints (optionally under a free root); other groups, and worlds with more cache-eligible active bodies than propagation_cached_response_body_max, keep the tree walk, selected per world on the device. Which is faster depends on the model.
options.when: Leave on; compare both on your model if the propagation sweep dominates.

options.name: propagation_cached_response_body_max
options.doc: Capacity of the cached responses in contact-active bodies of cache-eligible articulations per world; free bodies do not count. At least 1.
options.when: Raise when many contact-active bodies per world fall back to the tree walk.

options.name: propagation_color_order
options.doc: Order in which solve_mode="colored" colors a world's contacts and runs those left without a batch: "contact" (default) by contact index, or "longest_first" by row count, longest first, then contact index. A batch takes as long as its longest contact, so "longest_first" puts long contacts together, which shortens the sweep where one body carries many contacts with different row counts; on some stacked scenes it converges more slowly at a fixed iteration count. "rotating" walks the contact-index order in a different deterministic permutation every step. Gauss-Seidel favours the contacts it solves last, so a fixed order over a sorted contact stream (CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True) or contact matching) can favour the same contacts every step and twist a symmetric grasp; rotating spreads that over the contacts. Equal contact streams and step counts give equal orders; reproducible runs still need deterministic and a deterministic pipeline. It supports fewer than 1,048,583 propagation rows per world. solve_mode="serial" ignores it.
options.when: "rotating" spreads Gauss-Seidel bias over a symmetric grasp on a sorted contact stream; "longest_first" can shorten sweeps with uneven row counts.

options.name: friction_combine
options.doc: How a contact combines its two shapes' friction coefficients: "average", "min", "multiply" or "max", as PhysX's material combine modes. It applies to sliding friction (shape_material_mu); the free-body angular rows keep the larger coefficient of the pair under every mode. A contact with one shape keeps that shape's coefficient. Construction-only.
options.when: Match the combine mode of the engine you are porting from (PhysX average, min, multiply or max).

options.name: restitution_combine
options.doc: How a contact combines its two shapes' restitution coefficients, with the same modes as friction_combine, after each coefficient is clamped to [0, 1]. Construction-only.
options.when: Match the combine mode of the engine you are porting from.

options.name: free_rigid_torsional_friction
options.doc: Experimental torsional coefficient [m] for every free-body contact, replacing the shapes' steel:condim gate and shape_material_mu_torsional for that coefficient only; None keeps the shape data. Meant for sweeps that cannot edit shape data. Construction-only.
options.when: Sweeps over spin friction of free bodies without editing shapes.

options.name: free_rigid_rolling_friction
options.doc: Experimental rolling coefficient [m] for every free-body contact, replacing the shapes' steel:condim gate and shape_material_mu_rolling for that coefficient only; None keeps the shape data. Construction-only.
options.when: Sweeps over rolling friction of free bodies without editing shapes.

options.name: deterministic
options.doc: Run-to-run determinism of the solve. Pass a DeterministicMode, or None (default) to inherit wp.config.deterministic, which defaults to NOT_GUARANTEED. With RUN_TO_RUN the solver reserves its constraint rows in a fixed order instead of the order in which GPU threads reach the per-world row counters: joint rows in articulation order, contact rows in contact-buffer order within each world. Given identical inputs, including identically ordered contacts, repeated runs are then bitwise identical on the same GPU model, driver and Warp build, eagerly and under CUDA graph replay; combine it with CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True) for a reproducible contact order (see :ref:`Deterministic Contacts`). A world that overflows a row capacity keeps the rows of its earliest contacts and drops the rest, so unchanged inputs drop the same contacts every step; overflowed steps remain flagged in constraint_overflow. The mode adds a per-step sort of the contacts by world and row family and 24 bytes of storage per contact slot. With the "propagation" response it also lists each world's contact-active bodies by body index and sums each body's warm-start seed in row order. The seed walks a world's rows serially, so its cost grows with the contact rows in one world; solve_mode="colored" regroups a world's contact rows by color, an order fixed by the contact set. GPU_TO_GPU is not supported: passing it raises ValueError, and an inherited one emits a NewtonWarning and runs RUN_TO_RUN. deterministic reports the mode that runs, after any fallback. BODY_PARENT_F sums contact wrenches with atomics, so it is outside this guarantee. Steel's kernel modules always opt out of Warp's deterministic module option, so a process-wide wp.config.deterministic only selects this mode.
options.when: Set wp.DeterministicMode.RUN_TO_RUN for tests, debugging and data generation that must reproduce bit for bit. Pair it with CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True).

options.name: nesterov_momentum
options.doc: Accelerate the matrix-free Gauss-Seidel sweep with Nesterov momentum and O'Donoghue-Candes gradient restart, as in MuJoCo's PGS solver. Each sweep starts from the impulses extrapolated along the previous sweep's change, applied to the velocity through each row's response; momentum restarts when a sweep's correction opposes the extrapolation. Converges in fewer iterations on stacks, mass ratios and long chains; gains appear above a few iterations. The velocity_iterations post-pass runs the same sweep. Every world then runs the general sweep, bypassing the specialized sparse, local and paired-factor solves, and keeps 8 * (articulation_constraint_max + free_body_constraint_max) bytes of sweep history per world. Requires solve_mode="serial", articulated_contact_response="immediate" and row_schedule="interleaved"; other combinations raise ValueError. CUDA only: on CPU it raises NotImplementedError. Construction-only.
options.when: Resting stacks with mass ratios of roughly 100:1 to 1000:1 and long chains, when more iterations alone are too slow. Serial sweep, immediate response, CUDA only.

attributes.name: steel:rigid_body_angular_damping
attributes.doc: damps the angular velocity of free bodies and floating bases as w *= max(1 - d dt, 0) each step (physxRigidBody:angularDamping, default 0.05, as SolverFeatherstone); joints with a parent body are not damped. Fill the attribute for one value on every body.

attributes.name: steel:rigid_body_linear_damping
attributes.doc: damps the COM velocity of the same bodies as v *= max(1 - d dt, 0) each step (physxRigidBody:linearDamping, default 0). Keep it nonnegative.

attributes.name: steel:rigid_body_max_linear_velocity
attributes.doc: bound the velocity of free bodies (physxRigidBody:maxLinearVelocity and physxRigidBody:maxAngularVelocity, default unbounded).

attributes.name: steel:rigid_body_max_angular_velocity
attributes.doc: bound the velocity of free bodies (physxRigidBody:maxLinearVelocity and physxRigidBody:maxAngularVelocity, default unbounded).

attributes.name: steel:min_torsional_patch_radius
attributes.doc: is the effective spin radius of the shape's contacts (physxCollision:minTorsionalPatchRadius, default 0, no torsion). PhysX also scales a radius with the penetration depth through physxCollision:torsionalPatchRadius; this solver does not.

attributes.name: steel:condim
attributes.doc: (default 3) borrows MuJoCo's 3/4/6 convention; other values raise ValueError. At 4 a shape contributes shape_material_mu_torsional [m] to a spin row bounded by that coefficient times the normal load; at 6 also shape_material_mu_rolling [m] to a rolling pair. A contact takes the larger coefficient of its two shapes, regardless of the other shape's condim. Only contacts between free bodies, and free bodies on static or kinematic geometry, read it. USD reads it only from an explicitly authored newton:steel:condim; the MJCF importer leaves it to SolverMuJoCo's mujoco:condim. Under friction patches, contacts share a patch only if their angular coefficients match. A contact with angular rows takes up to 6 free-body rows instead of 3; raise free_body_constraint_max if constraint_overflow reports dropped rows. The solver reads steel:condim at construction and, on a solver built with the rows, at notify_model_changed with SHAPE_PROPERTIES; a solver built without any condim above 3 ignores the attribute and must be rebuilt to gain the rows. A negative or non-finite coefficient that a shape's condim enables raises ValueError at the same points.

attributes.name: steel:adhesion
attributes.doc: (default 0) is the pull of each contact point of the shape, MuJoCo's geom adhesion, which the MJCF importer reads. A contact pulls with the sum of its two shapes' values while it is within the pair's gap, so a gap makes shapes attract at a distance. The solver applies the pull A dt to the contact's normal row and solves its impulse in the unchanged contact cone, so the net normal impulse can reach -A dt, friction is bounded by mu times the net normal impulse plus A dt, and resting penetration is unchanged. Pull-off grows with the number of contact points of the pair. Within the gap, friction stays bounded by the solved impulse, which is zero until the pull would close the gap within the step (MuJoCo removes friction there). contact_f and body_parent_f report the net force. The solver reads the values every step, so writing zero releases a contact and writing the value engages it again, also between graph replays (a captured step keeps the array it was captured with, so recapture after replacing it); a solver built without a positive value ignores the attribute and must be rebuilt to gain adhesion. Construction and notify_model_changed with SHAPE_PROPERTIES raise ValueError for a negative or non-finite value. Adhesion keeps the dense mass factors and raises NotImplementedError with enable_sleeping, contact_compliance, contact_regularization > 0 and contact torsion. Experimental.steel:adhesion, its USD name newton:steel:adhesion and its contact law may change without the normal deprecation period.

attributes.name: steel:rigid_body_max_depenetration_velocity
attributes.doc: bounds the contact correction velocity of free bodies (physxRigidBody:maxDepenetrationVelocity, default unbounded).

attributes.name: steel:joint_friction_load_coefficient
attributes.doc: adds c (|F| + |T|) to the DOF's joint_friction (default 0). F [N] and T [N·m] are the force and the torque about the child body's center of mass that the joint transmits to its child's subtree under the step's free dynamics: gravity, applied body and joint forces, velocity-dependent terms and the resulting accelerations, before contacts, limits, friction and drive_mode="rows" drives act. T keeps its component about the joint axis, so a joint's own applied effort raises its friction. This is the joint friction law of PhysX articulations before PhysX 5.6, and the sum mixes units as it does there. USD reads it only from an explicitly authored newton:steel:jointFrictionLoadCoefficient, not from physxJoint:jointFriction, because the rows interact with drives differently from PhysX. The earlier spelling newton:steel:joint_friction_load_coefficient is read with a NewtonDeprecationWarning when the current name is not authored. Experimental.steel:joint_friction_load_coefficient, its USD name newton:steel:jointFrictionLoadCoefficient and its load law may change without the normal deprecation period.

inputs.name: Contacts.rigid_contact_match_generation
inputs.context: History carries across one collision pass into the same Contacts buffer when that pass matched against the solved contact set (rigid_contact_match_generation); a different buffer, skipped passes, or a pass after the pipeline wrote another buffer start cold.

inputs.name: Contacts.rigid_contact_match_index
inputs.context: Start each step from the previous step's contact impulses, matched by contact identity through rigid_contact_match_index, so the CollisionPipeline must be created with contact matching enabled.

inputs.name: Contacts.rigid_contact_stiffness
inputs.context: Experimental: solve contacts that carry a positive rigid_contact_stiffness [N/m] with an implicit unilateral spring-damper law instead of the rigid normal law.

inputs.name: Control.joint_f
inputs.context: A closure has no joint coordinate, so the limits, drive gains, damping, armature, velocity limit and joint_f of a loop-closing REVOLUTE joint's DOF are ignored.

inputs.name: Model.joint_X_c
inputs.context: The closure rows read joint_enabled, joint_X_p / joint_X_c and, for a REVOLUTE closure, joint_axis every step, so a closure is released, engaged, re-anchored or re-aimed by editing those arrays in place, also from a kernel between CUDA graph replays.

inputs.name: Model.joint_X_p
inputs.context: The closure rows read joint_enabled, joint_X_p / joint_X_c and, for a REVOLUTE closure, joint_axis every step, so a closure is released, engaged, re-anchored or re-aimed by editing those arrays in place, also from a kernel between CUDA graph replays.

inputs.name: Model.joint_armature
inputs.context: joint_armature and joint_damping are applied.

inputs.name: Model.joint_axis
inputs.context: The closure rows read joint_enabled, joint_X_p / joint_X_c and, for a REVOLUTE closure, joint_axis every step, so a closure is released, engaged, re-anchored or re-aimed by editing those arrays in place, also from a kernel between CUDA graph replays.

inputs.name: Model.joint_damping
inputs.context: joint_armature and joint_damping are applied.

inputs.name: Model.joint_effort_limit
inputs.context: By default (drive_mode="augmented") they are integrated implicitly by folding dt * kd + dt^2 * ke into the mass matrix; only the explicit drive force is clamped to joint_effort_limit, and the implicit stiffness and damping response is unbounded, so under a large external load the drive reaction can exceed the limit.

inputs.name: Model.joint_enabled
inputs.context: The closure rows read joint_enabled, joint_X_p / joint_X_c and, for a REVOLUTE closure, joint_axis every step, so a closure is released, engaged, re-anchored or re-aimed by editing those arrays in place, also from a kernel between CUDA graph replays.

inputs.name: Model.joint_friction
inputs.context: Experimental dry joint friction: with enable_joint_friction=True, joint_friction of PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE, BALL and D6 DOFs bounds one row per DOF.

inputs.name: Model.joint_limit_lower
inputs.context: Joint limits: with enable_joint_limits=True, every finite joint_limit_lower / joint_limit_upper of a PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE or D6 DOF is a unilateral row.

inputs.name: Model.joint_limit_upper
inputs.context: Joint limits: with enable_joint_limits=True, every finite joint_limit_lower / joint_limit_upper of a PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE or D6 DOF is a unilateral row.

inputs.name: Model.joint_rest_q
inputs.context: Passive joint springs: joint_stiffness and joint_rest_q on PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE and D6 DOFs, applied explicitly as stiffness * (rest_q - q) like SolverFeatherstone, independently of drives and joint limits.

inputs.name: Model.joint_stiffness
inputs.context: Passive joint springs: joint_stiffness and joint_rest_q on PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE and D6 DOFs, applied explicitly as stiffness * (rest_q - q) like SolverFeatherstone, independently of drives and joint limits.

inputs.name: Model.joint_target_kd
inputs.context: Joint drives: joint_target_ke and joint_target_kd on PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE and D6 DOFs.

inputs.name: Model.joint_target_ke
inputs.context: Joint drives: joint_target_ke and joint_target_kd on PRISMATIC, REVOLUTE and D6 DOFs.

inputs.name: Model.joint_velocity_limit
inputs.context: Joint velocity limits (joint_velocity_limit) are enforced as rows when enable_joint_velocity_limits is set.

inputs.name: Model.shape_material_mu
inputs.context: Non-negative factor applied to every shape's friction coefficient (shape_material_mu) in the solver's copy of the materials, refreshed at construction and by notify_model_changed with SHAPE_PROPERTIES.

inputs.name: Model.shape_material_mu_rolling
inputs.context: Experimental rolling coefficient [m] for every free-body contact, replacing the shapes' steel:condim gate and shape_material_mu_rolling for that coefficient only;

inputs.name: Model.shape_material_mu_torsional
inputs.context: Experimental torsional coefficient [m] for every free-body contact, replacing the shapes' steel:condim gate and shape_material_mu_torsional for that coefficient only;

inputs.name: ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig.gap
inputs.context: gap decides which contacts the pipeline reports (also to sensors and other solvers); this gate only decides which of them this solver solves.

inputs.name: ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig.restitution
inputs.context: Restitution follows the shapes' restitution.

inputs.name: State.body_f
inputs.context: …solved motion: inverse dynamics with the post-solve joint accelerations (taken from the velocities the dynamics start from, after any velocity-limit prescaling), less gravity, body_f, and the solved impulses divided by dt of the subtree's contact normal, friction and spin rows and its loop-closure…

inputs.name: State.joint_q
inputs.context: Like SolverFeatherstone, the solver uses joint_q and joint_qd as its state and does not simulate bodies that are not connected through joints.

inputs.name: State.joint_qd
inputs.context: Like SolverFeatherstone, the solver uses joint_q and joint_qd as its state and does not simulate bodies that are not connected through joints.

methods.name: register_custom_attributes
methods.doc: Register the body, shape and joint DOF attributes consumed by Steel in the steel namespace.

methods.name: velocity_limits_fused
methods.doc: Whether the fused velocity-limit clamp is active: fuse_joint_velocity_limits applies only with drive rows and joint velocity limits.

methods.name: supported_observables
methods.doc: Return the observables available for this configuration; BODY_AWAKE requires enable_sleeping.

methods.name: observables
methods.doc: Allocate observable arrays; body_awake starts with the solver's current flags.

methods.name: notify_model_changed
methods.doc: Refresh cached solver data after model changes.

methods.name: notify_state_changed
methods.doc: Drop the carried kinematics of the selected worlds after writing state outside step.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Clear solver-owned state of the selected worlds.

methods.name: step
methods.doc: Advance the simulation by one time step.

methods.name: constraint_row_watermarks
methods.doc: Return the row high-water marks accumulated since construction (row_watermark only).

methods.name: compliance_contact_count
methods.doc: Compliant contacts prepared by the last step (contact_compliance only).

methods.name: compliance_skipped_contact_count
methods.doc: Positive-stiffness contacts the row allocator excluded in the last step (contact_compliance only).

methods.name: snapshot_constraint_status
methods.doc: Copy the status that check_constraint_capacity reports on the device, without waiting.

methods.name: check_constraint_capacity
methods.doc: Raise if any world or the global entry lost contacts or rows, or rejected input, since its last reset.

methods.name: check_joint_friction
methods.doc: Raise if a step read invalid joint friction, or if check_constraint_capacity raises.

methods.name: validate_contact_compliance
methods.doc: Raise if contact compliance rejected its input, or if check_constraint_capacity raises.

methods.name: joint_friction_invalid
methods.doc: Per-world device flags, global entry last, for invalid joint friction read by a step.

methods.name: joint_qd_public_convention
methods.doc: True: free-joint joint_qd is (v_com_world, omega_world), as eval_fk reads it.
